Search focus: Identification, procedure matching, communication, language, accessibility, patient partnership
Key evidence conclusion: Identity and proposed procedure/site/side require confirmation. Communication should be tailored to language, literacy and accessibility needs, with accredited interpreters available when required.
Dataset change: Preferred name reclassified as UX/contextual rather than clinical M0. Interpreter/language/accessibility follow-up logic strengthened.
Primary sources: ANZCA PG07; ACSQHC Partnering with Consumers; ACSQHC Communicating for Safety; Ahmadian core dataset
Next action: Consumer review of wording and digital accessibility testing

Search focus: Current symptoms, deterioration, infection, recent admissions, medication/diagnostic changes
Key evidence conclusion: Preoperative information must reflect current health. Significant elapsed time or change in comorbidity warrants reassessment. Active/new cardiopulmonary or infectious symptoms require escalation rather than silent completion.
Dataset change: Added explicit deterioration/infection escalation. COVID-specific timing moved out of static dataset into versioned rules layer. Some duplicate recent-change fields made conditional.
Primary sources: ANZCA PG07; RCoA GPAS Chapter 2; Canadian Guidelines to Practice of Anesthesia; contemporary SARS-CoV-2 guidance
Next action: Later cross-check with respiratory and medication domains

Search focus: Known CVD, risk factors, active symptoms, HF, arrhythmia, devices, pulmonary hypertension
Key evidence conclusion: Guidelines support accurate history focused on established CVD, cardiovascular risk factors and symptoms. Newly detected chest pain, dyspnoea, oedema and concerning syncope require further assessment. Active HF symptoms confer higher risk than compensated HF.
Dataset change: Strengthened red-flag logic for chest pain, syncope, palpitations and HF symptoms. Recent admissions/investigations remain conditional branches.
Primary sources: 2024 AHA/ACC multisociety guideline; 2022 ESC NCS guideline; ANZCA PG07
Next action: Later map cardiac conditions to RCRI/other deterministic risk inputs

Search focus: DASI, METS study, stair-climbing, poor/indeterminate functional capacity
Key evidence conclusion: Structured functional assessment such as DASI is reasonable in elevated-risk surgery. Subjective clinician estimates perform less well than DASI in major surgery. DASI ≤34 has prognostic significance in elevated-risk cohorts.
Dataset change: Full DASI activity set changed from universal M0 to conditional C4. Brief functional screen retained where clinically relevant, with structured DASI triggered by elevated risk or poor/indeterminate capacity.
Primary sources: 2024 AHA/ACC multisociety guideline; 2022 ESC NCS guideline; METS study; DASI threshold cohort
Next action: Confirm licensing/wording requirements before reproducing DASI verbatim in production

Search focus: Asthma/COPD/other lung disease, symptoms, exacerbation, respiratory support, PPC risk
Key evidence conclusion: Pulmonary evaluation should focus on clinically significant lung disease, current symptoms and control, recent respiratory infection/exacerbation and severity markers. ARISCAT uses SpO2 and recent respiratory infection among its predictors.
Dataset change: Changed individual chronic lung diagnoses from universal questions to condition-triggered branches after a broad respiratory screen. Dyspnoea remains universal; wheeze/cough and severity fields are conditional.
Primary sources: Contemporary pulmonary evaluation review; ARISCAT/PPC literature
Next action: Cross-check smoking in PSY domain and measured SpO2 in observations/integration layer

Search focus: Known OSA, STOP-Bang, PAP use/adherence, sleep study
Key evidence conclusion: SASM recommends identifying surgical patients at risk of OSA and supports validated screening tools including STOP-Bang. CPOC 2025 recommends routine screening and risk stratification of patients without an existing diagnosis.
Dataset change: Retained universal OSA screening but removed unnecessary re-asking of age/hypertension. Neck circumference is measure/availability-dependent. PAP details remain conditional for known OSA.
Primary sources: SASM OSA guideline; CPOC OSA guidance 2025
Next action: Confirm exact STOP-Bang licensing/implementation and avoid duplicate demographic questions

Search focus: Stroke/TIA, epilepsy, Parkinson disease, neuromuscular disease, baseline deficits and dysphagia
Key evidence conclusion: Detailed neurological assessment is most useful after a broad positive neurological history. Recent cerebrovascular events, poorly controlled seizures and significant neuromuscular disease materially alter perioperative planning. Neuromuscular disorders require assessment of weakness plus respiratory, bulbar and cardiac involvement.
Dataset change: Changed disease-by-disease questions from universal to conditional branches. Strengthened stroke/TIA, seizure, dysphagia and neuromuscular escalation/follow-up logic.
Primary sources: AHA/ASA perioperative stroke statement; preoperative neurological evaluation review; ENMC neuromuscular consensus
Next action: Cross-map cognition/delirium to RES domain and time-critical neurological medicines to MED

Search focus: CKD, AKI, dialysis, access, transplant, fluid/electrolyte issues
Key evidence conclusion: CKD and diabetes are important PO-AKI risk states and risk-based kidney health assessment is recommended. Dialysis patients require detailed pre-anaesthetic assessment, with particular attention to recent dialysis, volume/electrolytes and vascular access.
Dataset change: Kept CKD/dialysis/transplant screening universal but made detailed stage/schedule/access/electrolyte fields conditional. Laboratory eGFR/creatinine and electrolyte data are preferentially sourced from records rather than patient recall.
Primary sources: ADQI/POQI PO-AKI consensus; chronic dialysis anaesthesia review; ESRD/CKD preoperative review
Next action: Later map current creatinine/eGFR/electrolytes from EMR/labs rather than conversation

Search focus: Diabetes type/control, insulin technology, hypoglycaemia/DKA, thyroid/adrenal/pituitary disease, steroid exposure
Key evidence conclusion: Diabetes history requires type, treatment and recent acute complications. SGLT2 and GLP-1/GIP therapies have specific perioperative implications but management recommendations are version-sensitive and belong in the medication rules layer. Australian 2025 guidance explicitly recommends asking all patients about GLP-1/GIP use.
Dataset change: Detailed diabetes fields remain condition-triggered. Thyroid/adrenal/pituitary diagnoses moved behind a broad endocrine screen. Chronic steroid exposure remains an important targeted screen. Added explicit cross-domain requirement that GLP-1/GIP and SGLT2 use be resolved in MED, including non-diabetic use.
Primary sources: ADA Standards 2026; 2025 ADS/ANZCA/GESA/NACOS GLP-1/GIP recommendations
Next action: Ensure MED domain contains explicit SGLT2 and GLP-1/GIP concepts and versioned management rules

Search focus: Reflux, dysphagia, regurgitation, gastroparesis, vomiting/obstruction, liver disease/decompensation
Key evidence conclusion: Aspiration risk is driven by active symptoms and conditions affecting gastric emptying/regurgitation as well as fasting status. Fasting compliance should be checked close to the procedure rather than treated as static history. Liver disease requires identification of decompensation features.
Dataset change: Dysphagia and persistent nausea/vomiting retained as high-priority screens. Hiatus hernia/gastroparesis made conditional. Strengthened obstruction and hepatic decompensation escalation. GLP-1/GIP exposure cross-links to aspiration rules.
Primary sources: ASA fasting/aspiration guidance; 2025 Australian GLP-1/GIP recommendations; contemporary cirrhosis perioperative guidance
Next action: Create separate day-of-procedure fasting/full-stomach safety state in logic specification

Search focus: Anaemia/PBM, bleeding phenotype, VTE, anticoagulants/antiplatelets, transfusion and blood preferences
Key evidence conclusion: PBM emphasises detection/treatment of anaemia and identification of bleeding risk. Antithrombotic medicines must be identified precisely, but interruption/resumption is procedure-, indication-, renal-function- and drug-dependent. Blood-product preferences must be individualised.
Dataset change: Strengthened source priority for laboratory Hb. Exact antithrombotic drug/dose/indication/last dose required with no cessation advice from the history model. Transfusion history made conditional while blood-product restriction remains mandatory where transfusion could be relevant.
Primary sources: National Blood Authority PBM; ICCAMS; CHEST perioperative antithrombotic guideline
Next action: Cross-map anticoagulants/antiplatelets to MED and build separate antithrombotic rules engine

Search focus: Prior anaesthesia types, difficult airway, awareness, PONV, delayed emergence, ICU/ventilation, hypersensitivity and record retrieval
Key evidence conclusion: Previous anaesthetic experience and complications are core pre-anaesthesia history. Safety-critical prior events require record retrieval where possible. Detailed complication questions should only activate after prior anaesthetic exposure or a reported problem.
Dataset change: Changed multiple complication questions from universal M0 to C1 after prior anaesthesia/problem screen. Strengthened mandatory review and record retrieval for difficult airway, awareness, prolonged ventilation and perioperative hypersensitivity.
Primary sources: ANZCA PG07; ASA Basic Standards for Preanesthesia Care; 2025 MH guidance
Next action: Cross-check with Family Anaesthetic History, Airway and Allergy domains

Search focus: MH, anaesthetic death, prolonged paralysis/apnoea, RYR1/heat/exercise phenotype
Key evidence conclusion: Family history is important for inherited anaesthetic risks, particularly MH. A broad family anaesthetic-problem screen should trigger targeted MH/prolonged paralysis questions; previous uneventful anaesthesia does not exclude MH susceptibility.
Dataset change: Retained one universal broad family screen and changed specific MH/death/paralysis/genetic questions to conditional branches. Strengthened mandatory review for known family MH/RYR1 findings.
Primary sources: 2025 JSA MH guideline; ANZCA PG07
Next action: Cross-link positive family MH to deterministic non-triggering-anaesthesia safety pathway

Search focus: Prior airway difficulty, mouth/neck restriction, head/neck surgery/radiotherapy, tracheostomy, dental vulnerability
Key evidence conclusion: Prior difficult/failed intubation is among the strongest historical predictors of future difficulty. Head/neck pathology, prior surgery/radiotherapy, reduced mouth opening and limited neck extension are relevant. Conversational history supplements but cannot replace physical airway examination.
Dataset change: Made airway-history questions anaesthetic/procedure-dependent rather than universally mandatory. Detailed head/neck branches activate on positive screen. Added explicit boundary that Mallampati/mouth opening/neck examination remains clinician-performed.
Primary sources: Difficult airway assessment consensus; DAS awake intubation guidance; ANZCA PG07
Next action: Later define structured handoff to clinician physical airway examination

Search focus: Medication reconciliation, high-risk omitted classes, GLP-1/GIP, SGLT2, antithrombotics, steroids, opioids, patches, supplements/OTC
Key evidence conclusion: A complete medication history should include prescription, OTC, herbal and complementary medicines. Medication reconciliation is a key perioperative safety intervention. High-risk classes require explicit resolution, but medication management rules should not be embedded in the LLM.
Dataset change: Converted medication details to repeatable Medication[] objects. Last dose is required when clinically/time relevant rather than for every low-risk medicine. Preserved explicit probes for commonly omitted/high-risk classes and made them skippable when already resolved by an authoritative current list plus patient confirmation.
Primary sources: ANZCA PG07; NSW ACI Perioperative Toolkit; 2025 medication-error systematic review; ANZCA GLP-1/GIP guidance
Next action: Build Medication[] object schema and medication-source reconciliation hierarchy

Search focus: Agent, reaction phenotype/timing/severity, treatment, re-exposure/testing, perioperative reaction, latex/chlorhexidine
Key evidence conclusion: ANZCA PG69 requires a comprehensive allergy history. Previous perioperative anaphylaxis is the strongest predictor of future perioperative anaphylaxis. Important triggers include neuromuscular blockers, antibiotics, latex, sugammadex and chlorhexidine; unresolved significant allergy warrants record review and possibly specialist referral.
Dataset change: Formalised repeatable Allergy[] object. Strengthened reaction phenotype, re-exposure and record retrieval. Retained explicit perioperative-reaction and chlorhexidine probes, with hidden-exposure logic. Unclear EMR allergy labels remain unresolved rather than being treated as negative.
Primary sources: ANZCA PG69 2025
Next action: Build Allergy[] object and contradiction/delabelling workflow; map to medication and device exposure

Domain: Frailty, cognition, nutrition and functional independence
Search focus: Frailty, ADL/IADL, falls, cognition/delirium, functional decline, weight loss/intake and nutrition
Key evidence conclusion: Older patients undergoing intermediate/high-risk surgery should be assessed for frailty with an established tool. Cognitive impairment is common and should be actively identified in risk groups. Nutrition guidance supports early nutritional-risk assessment and intervention in surgical patients at risk.
Dataset change: Detailed independence/cognition questions changed from broad M1 to C4 risk-triggered branches. Weight should preferentially come from measured/EMR data. Nutrition screen targeted to major surgery, frailty, low BMI, cancer/GI disease or recent illness.
Primary sources: RCoA GPAS Chapter 2; ESPEN Clinical Nutrition in Surgery Update 2025
Next action: Select validated frailty/cognition/nutrition instruments and confirm licensing/implementation

Domain: Pain, psychological health and substance use
Search focus: Chronic pain, OME, psychological risk, anxiety, smoking/vaping, alcohol and non-prescribed substances
Key evidence conclusion: Preoperative services should identify chronic pain, opioid exposure, psychological/anxiety factors and lifestyle risks. High-dose opioid exposure should be quantified, with OME recorded. Smoking, excess alcohol and drug use are relevant optimisation targets.
Dataset change: Retained universal chronic pain/opioid, smoking/vaping and alcohol screens. Converted individual psychiatric diagnoses and drug-by-drug recreational substance questions to conditional branches. OME remains deterministic.
Primary sources: RCoA GPAS Chapters 2 and 11; RCoA high-risk pain guidance
Next action: Choose concise validated alcohol/psychological tools for triggered pathways

Search focus: Home environment, supports, transport, escort/supervision, dependants, access and discharge barriers
Key evidence conclusion: Discharge planning should begin early so resources and obstacles can be addressed. Social suitability requirements vary by procedure, recovery burden and day-surgery pathway rather than being universal medical-history questions.
Dataset change: Most detailed social questions changed to procedure/discharge-triggered C2. Retained a general concern-about-managing-at-home screen for elective patients with recovery needs.
Primary sources: RCoA GPAS Chapter 2; RCoA Day Surgery guidance
Next action: Localise escort/supervision requirements to service policy rather than hard-code globally

Domain: Patient priorities, goals, advance care planning and reproductive considerations
Search focus: Goals, function, unacceptable outcomes, ACD/SDM/treatment limits, pregnancy/breastfeeding and information preferences
Key evidence conclusion: Shared decision making requires understanding patient goals and preferences, particularly for high-risk or preference-sensitive decisions. Advance-care questions are most relevant to high-risk/frail/seriously ill patients. Reproductive questions should be based on pregnancy potential and clinical relevance rather than demographic assumptions.
Dataset change: Goals/recovery retained for elective/major surgery. Advance-care fields changed to C4. Pregnancy possibility changed to pregnancy-potential/context trigger. Hormonal contraception cross-linked to Medication[] rather than duplicated. Information/decision-style preferences made optional UX fields.
Primary sources: RCoA GPAS Chapter 2 and shared decision-making principles
Next action: Align reproductive workflow with local SA Health pregnancy-testing policy and consent requirements
